note: Foundational groove. Every other hip-hop step in the curriculum sits on top of this one, so it is taught first and drilled longest.

measurability.rationale: The movement IS detected reliably — every measured take clears this step's own phase gates (knee extension >168 deg before each dip, descent and rise above 40 deg/s, dips at least 6 deg deep: 100% of dips in all three reference sources). What tier A additionally claimed, and the data does not support, is that a learner can be scored against instructor consensus: the teachers we measured agree more tightly than our own measurement noise, so the tolerance band is mostly our caution rather than their agreement.

evidence: median joint tolerance is 83% floor-derived (MIN_TOLERANCE_DEG = 6.0 deg), against 28% / 9% / 22% for the accepted references (salsa shine / Running Man / Roger Rabbit) — 3-9x their share
the same round measured the opposite for detection: this step's `top` gate (>168 deg) was met by 100% of dips in all three sources
tierWithdrawn.note: DETECTION and SCORABILITY are separate claims and this withdrawal touches only the second. Reading it as 'the bounce cannot be measured' would be wrong — it is measured; what cannot be done is grading a learner against a consensus that sits below our own resolution.

promotionPath.blockedBy: instructor disagreement below the 6.0 deg noise floor at 3 sources
promotionPath.unblockedBy: a rebuild with >=6 independent teachers in which measured disagreement exceeds the floor — i.e. the median floor-derived share falls into the 9-28% band the accepted references occupy. The tier question reopens with THAT data, not with an opinion.

cycleUnit.rationale: The phase chain is top -> drop -> bottom -> rise with `rise` terminal, so one cycle contains exactly ONE knee dip. Consistent with beats:1 and countLabels:['1']. This is DECLARED, not inferred by the segment finder: a 2x spread in measured period between two takes of this step is a TEMPO difference between instructors, not a unit disagreement — the unit is fixed here (M-F-231).
cycleUnit.note: Steps whose phases are driven by cyclePhaseNear rather than a kinematic metric declare no cycleUnit; those keep the ankle-anchored segment path unchanged.

scoring.freeJointsRationale: Arm styling over a bounce is personal expression, not technique. Scoring it would penalise the learner for having a style — plan C-014.

errors.note: The learner is standing still to the music. The single most common beginner failure and the reason this step is level 1.

Hip-hop groove sits DOWN on the beat. Bottoming out on the 'and' is a genuine style error, not a timing miss — the shape is right and the phase is wrong, so it must be named differently from STEP_LATE.
Bending at the waist instead of the knees. Detected as a conjunction so that a deliberate forward-leaning groove is not flagged.

reference.note: ≥3 independent instructors required, 6 preferred — catalogue §6.0. Tolerance is derived from their disagreement, not authored. Built 2026-08-04 from 1IVtcoqMrBA / 4BRd2E8vBic / DEWpw4n8Lkw; carries cycleUnit (knee_flexion_mean, 1 dip per cycle) and four NAMED exclusions in decisions.json (no-speech / amplitude-floor / camera-driver-disjoint / identity).
reference.notConsumedForScoring: The artifact exists and is kept, but nothing grades against it while this step is demoOnly — it is the record of what was measured, and the baseline any future >=6-source rebuild is compared to. Deleting it would throw away the evidence the tier decision rests on.
